Reweight a cohort survey design

Source: R/reweight.R
nis_reweight.Rd

Multiply the cohort's discharge weights by prespecified analysis factors.

Usage

nis_reweight(design, weights)

Arguments

design

A result of nis_design(). Column selection, renaming, and mutation are supported when cohort rows are unchanged. Required internal design fields are restored from survey metadata; removed analysis columns are not restored.

weights

Numeric weights aligned with the cohort rows of design, or an unquoted numeric column name in the design data. They are matched to rows by position, so take them from design$variables in that order (for example, fit the propensity model on design$variables) and do not reorder or subset the rows first.

Value

A filtered srvyr::tbl_svy survey design.

Details

The design retains the original hospital and stratum structure. Uncertainty estimates treat the supplied factors as fixed.

See also

Make tables and fit survey models, Make tables and fit survey models.

Other survey-design: nis_design(), nis_design_report(), nis_survey()

Examples

nis <- nis_open(nis_example(2019:2020))
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpBWClEw/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
#> duckdb keeps downloaded extensions and secrets in a temporary directory:
#> ℹ /tmp/RtmpBWClEw/duckdb
#> This is removed when the R session ends.
#> • Extensions are re-downloaded each session.
#> • Secrets are lost.
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = TRUE) (or create ~/.duckdb) to keep them (suitable for most users).
#> ℹ Run duckdb(shared_home = FALSE) to accept the temporary directory (and silence this message).
#> ℹ See ?duckdb_storage for details and alternatives.
design <- nis_design(nis, AGE >= 18, keep = c(AGE, LOS))
#> Preparing the cohort survey design.
reweighted <- nis_reweight(design, ifelse(AGE >= 65, 1.2, 0.9))
srvyr::summarise(reweighted, mean_los = srvyr::survey_mean(LOS))
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   mean_los mean_los_se
#>      <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1     5.41       0.151
